minutes.headline: Board adopted extra retiree COLA and committed more money for the delayed, over-budget property revaluation.
minutes.summary: The board heard water and sewer officials argue for ARPA funds, voted to accept the retiree COLA provision, and ratified two appointments. Most of the meeting was a pointed discussion of why the five-year revaluation bid came in late and over budget, ending in a vote to commit additional funds so the contract can be awarded.

public_comment.stated_role: chairman of the board of water Commissioners
public_comment.topic: Offered written answers to board questions on the water district's ARPA request; board asked for an emailed response.
Offered to present on the retiree COLA and the Worcester County Retirement vote count.

Argued the sewer department's ARPA request merits the same treatment as the water district's, citing new permit requirements, flood studies and covid-driven flow; board treated it as a communication and asked for a modified request.

votes.motion: Accept the provisions of Chapter 269 of the Acts of 2022 giving an additional two percent cost of living increase to eligible Worcester Regional retirement retirees, retroactive to July 1, 2022.
Ratify the town manager's appointment of James Ricci as on-call firefighter/EMT.
Ratify the town manager's appointment of Ashley Denio as conservation administrative assistant.
Approve minutes of March 21 and March 28, 2023 as written.
Commit thirty thousand dollars for the fiscal 24 tax revaluation.

budget_items.topic: Sewer enterprise retained earnings and ARPA request
budget_items.what_was_said: Sewer commission chair said it requests an ARPA amount and had retained earnings at end of 2022, with a planned draw for operations.
A retiree said the COLA applies only to the first portion of a pension, with a stated maximum benefit.
Board reviewed several warrants including payroll, payroll deduction, real estate refund and teachers lump sum.
A single proposal came in well above what the budget held for the five-year revaluation, and the vendor could not start until October.
Board discussed cash flow and possible short-term borrowing if tax bills are delayed.
Prior ARPA allocation for the investigation was largely expended, with more payroll still to be calculated.
Town manager said the gap to award the contract is about seventy thousand, partly covered by existing funds; board committed the rest from ARPA.

transfers.description: Additional ARPA allocation for FY24 revaluation, raising the earlier allocation total

decisions.decision: Water district chair to email written answers on ARPA to the town manager for distribution; joint meeting possible if confusion remains.
Sewer Commission invited to submit a modified ARPA request with added context on unexpected costs before the July 11 meeting.
Board aims to decide the remaining ARPA allotment around mid-July.
Liaison and committee assignments, MRPC representative and master planning volunteer deferred until a full board.
Board will ask the board of assessors for its annual agenda going forward; cannot compel it.
Next meeting July 11, then July 18; no meeting in the coming week.

what_happened.line: The board voted to commit additional funds for the fiscal 24 tax revaluation so the contract can be awarded after a single bid came in over budget.
The town manager said the shortfall to award the revaluation contract was partly covered by existing funds, with the rest committed from ARPA.
The board voted to accept Chapter 269 of the Acts of 2022, an additional cost of living increase for eligible Worcester Regional retirees, retroactive to July 1, 2022.
Sewer officials asked for ARPA funds on par with the water district's request; the board asked for a modified request with added context before July 11.
The board ratified the town manager's appointments of an on-call firefighter/EMT and a conservation administrative assistant.

why_it_matters: Revaluation sets the assessed values that tax bills are based on, and its cost now draws on ARPA money that is no longer available for other town needs.
Accepting the retiree COLA provision adds to what the town owes through its share of the regional retirement system, which is paid out of the town budget.
The water and sewer ARPA requests compete for a limited remaining allotment, so the board's mid-July decision determines what is left for other uses.
watch_next: July 11 Select Board meeting: sewer commission's modified ARPA request due, and the remaining ARPA allotment is expected to be decided around mid-July.
Liaison and committee assignments, the MRPC representative and a master planning volunteer, deferred until a full board is seated.
